testTitle: Converze.AI Public Portal - Scenario 6: 12 Users, Mixed Survey (2 Support + 2 Oppose) & Balanced Pros/Oppose Questions Validation
articleTitle: The US$6.3 billion Binance hack is the biggest heist ever – it should be a wake up call for cryptocurrency users

support.text: Cryptocurrency exchanges should fully reimburse users for funds lost in security breaches.
People who keep their funds on an exchange share some responsibility when those funds are stolen.
Governments should require crypto exchanges to follow the same security standards as traditional banks.
Stricter government regulation of crypto exchanges would do more harm than good to the industry.
Exchanges should keep most user funds in offline storage, even if it makes withdrawals slower.
The convenience of trading on centralised exchanges outweighs the security risks they carry.
Ordinary people should not need technical knowledge to keep their cryptocurrency safe.
Crypto exchanges should be required to publish regular independent security audits for their users.
Blockchain technology itself is more secure than the companies and platforms built around it.
Cryptocurrency remains a reasonable investment choice for ordinary savers despite high-profile thefts.

oppose.text: Cryptocurrency exchanges should fully reimburse users for funds lost in security breaches.
People who keep their funds on an exchange share some responsibility when those funds are stolen.

Exchanges should keep most user funds in offline storage, even if it makes withdrawals slower.

Ordinary people should not need technical knowledge to keep their cryptocurrency safe.

Blockchain technology itself is more secure than the companies and platforms built around it.

criticalValidation.result: PASS - Both Pros AND Oppose questions delivered (expected for 2 Support + 2 Oppose mixed viewpoints)

detailedAudit.questionText: Does the Binance hack prove that even the world's largest exchange cannot be trusted to safeguard user funds?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Binance hack proves exchange untrustworthy

detailedAudit.questionText: Why frame this as a 'wake-up call for crypto users' when the underlying blockchains themselves were never breached?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Underlying blockchains were never breached

detailedAudit.questionText: If $6.3 billion can be drained in roughly 20 minutes, should users ever treat centralized exchanges as safe places to hold assets?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Centralized exchanges safe places to hold assets

detailedAudit.questionText: Doesn't Binance restoring 95% of assets within days and freezing another $3 billion show the industry's safety nets already worked?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Binance restoring assets shows safety nets work

detailedAudit.questionText: Does this attack vindicate the 'not your keys, not your coins' philosophy about self-custody?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Not your keys not your coins self custody

detailedAudit.questionText: Traditional banks and payment systems have suffered massive fraud and cyber losses too — is this really a uniquely crypto problem?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Traditional banks suffered massive fraud too

detailedAudit.questionText: Should all exchanges now be required to publish independent, third-party security audits of their withdrawal and signing infrastructure?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Exchanges required to publish independent security audits

detailedAudit.questionText: Isn't the real lesson that one company had an operational security lapse, not that cryptocurrency itself is unsafe?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: One company operational lapse not crypto unsafe

detailedAudit.questionText: Since Binance restored assets from its corporate treasury rather than recovering the stolen funds, does this suggest exchanges reuse or recycle customer deposits?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Exchanges reuse customer deposits

detailedAudit.questionText: Wouldn't heavy-handed regulation born from this incident punish the entire industry for a single exchange's failure?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Heavy-handed regulation punishes entire industry

detailedAudit.questionText: Should regulators mandate that a significant percentage of exchange reserves be held in audited cold storage?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Mandate exchange reserves in audited cold storage

detailedAudit.questionText: Shouldn't the blame fall on state-sponsored hackers, such as those linked to North Korea, rather than on crypto users' choices?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Blame fall on state-sponsored hackers

detailedAudit.questionText: Is it time for crypto exchanges to have bank-style deposit insurance backed by regulators rather than voluntary corporate funds?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Bank-style deposit insurance backed by regulators

detailedAudit.questionText: Doesn't the rapid freezing of stolen funds across multiple blockchains demonstrate that blockchain transparency is actually a security strength?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Freezing funds demonstrates blockchain transparency strength

detailedAudit.questionText: Should exchanges with compromised withdrawal systems be required to halt operations until independent audits confirm they are secure?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Halt operations until independent audits confirm secure

detailedAudit.questionText: Does this hack show that blockchain security and exchange security are fundamentally different, so users must stop conflating them?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Blockchain security and exchange security fundamentally different

detailedAudit.questionText: Is mass self-custody realistic when ordinary users routinely lose keys and fall for phishing scams?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Mass self-custody realistic when users lose keys

detailedAudit.questionText: Given suspected North Korean involvement, should there be stronger international coordination to freeze and recover state-linked crypto theft?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Stronger international coordination for state-linked crypto theft

detailedAudit.questionText: Isn't it premature to demand policy changes or pause features like EIP-7702 before attribution and root cause are fully established?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Premature to demand policy changes before root cause established

detailedAudit.questionText: Should multi-signature approvals and time-locks on large withdrawals become mandatory industry standards after this breach?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Multi-signature approvals and time-locks mandatory

detailedAudit.questionText: Why single out crypto for a 'wake-up call' when breaches happen across every financial system?
detailedAudit.matchedAdminText: Why single out crypto when breaches happen everywhere
